thesis: Land a commander, turn every draw (Shabraz) and every discard (Brallin) into +1/+1 counters, multiply the counters with draw doublers and Lae'zel and the damage with Torbran, Artist's Talent and Gratuitous Violence, then cash it as one double-striking, evasive hit for 21 commander damage. The wheels are the last fuel, not the key.

stages.label: RED FIRST, BLUE THIN
stages.what_it_does: Thirty-six lands (34 entries; Mountain is the only basic) plus six two-mana-or-less rocks, Smothering Tithe and Jeska's Will pay for a 4- or 5-mana commander and then for equip costs, double-strike tricks and a finishing wheel. The ramp group the goldfish declares (Sol Ring, Arcane Signet, two Signets, two Talismans, Smothering Tithe; 7 cards) is in 41.2% of opening sevens and drawn by turn six in 73.5% of games (deck-audit). deck-facts: land sources R 34 / U 23 / W 19 against targets R 36 / U 22 / W 22, 14 lands can enter tapped, and red carries 37 of the pips over 24 cards. Red and white both sit under their source targets and blue sits one over, so the lean toward red has not yet met red's own target. Opal Palace also puts extra +1/+1 counters on a commander recast with its mana, and Talon Gates of Madara can phase out a blocker; both are filed here because making mana is what they do every game.

evidence.note: Signets, Talismans, Sol Ring, Arcane Signet carry ramp:rock

stages.label: A COMMANDER ON THE TABLE
stages.what_it_does: Nothing in this deck starts itself any more: the engine is the commanders' own triggers, so the first thing that has to resolve is Shabraz (5 mana, flying; +1/+1 counter and 1 life per card you draw) or Brallin (4 mana; +1/+1 counter and 1 damage to each opponent per card you discard). Until one is on the battlefield every loot, wheel and doubler is just card flow. The two commanders also hand each other evasion by oracle text: Brallin's {R} gives a Shark trample and Shabraz is a Shark Bird; Shabraz's {W/U} gives a Human flying and Brallin is a Human Shaman. Two commanders means the ignition is redundant, not single, but each removal adds 2 to that commander's tax. goldfish_metrics.json (current list, 10,000 games) prices it directly. Shabraz is cast by turn six in 89.2% of games (mean turn 4.771, median 5), Brallin in 96.7% (mean 3.927). Both are out by turn four in 34.3% and by turn six in 88.7%. The goldfish casts each commander once and keeps it, with no removal, tax or recast, so read these as a ceiling on the ignition, not its survival. This is the stage the old model got wrong: v1 called the wheel the ignition, and goldfish_targets still marks the wheel `required`.

evidence.note: with both commanders out, seven discards are seven Brallin triggers and seven draws seven Shabraz triggers

stages.label: EVERY CARD THAT MOVES
stages.what_it_does: Each card drawn is a counter on Shabraz, each card discarded a counter on Brallin and a ping to every opponent, so a loot pays both commanders at once. Steady fuel: Faithless Looting, Frantic Search, Sorcerer Class, Collector's Vault, Kitsa, Teferi, Master of Time (a loot on any turn), Rielle, Rhystic Study, Mask of Memory. Bulk fuel is the eight full-hand wheels: four plain ones (Windfall, Tolarian Winds, Reforge the Soul, Jace's Archivist) and four that also deal damage (Collective Defiance, Fateful Showdown, Incendiary Command, Khorvath's Fury), plus Prismari Command's loot. Artist's Talent's loot is fuel too, but the card is filed under conversion, where its only stack-proven ability lives. The pilot's rule is that a wheel is cast with a commander already out, as the finishing turn. The wheel group is in 45.6% of opening sevens and drawn by turn six in 72.6% of games, mean turn 3.054 (deck-audit), so the usual job is holding one, not finding one. Idyllic Tutor is here as aimed card flow: its eight enchantment targets span four stages. There is no fodder stage: the deck eats its own hand, and no card in the 99 exists to be discarded.

evidence.note: Windfall for seven: 7 damage to each opponent (40 to 33), both commanders 10/10, 7 life
a discard paid as a cost (cycling) is still a discard for Brallin; Raugrin Triome and Marauding Mako cycle

stages.label: MAKE EACH CARD WORTH MORE
stages.what_it_does: The commanders convert one card into one counter, and these seven raise what each card is worth. Teferi's Ageless Insight, Bard, King of Dale and Alhammarret's Archive each turn an extra draw into two, so a wheel's draws and every loot's draws pay Shabraz twice. Lae'zel adds one to every placement of counters on your creatures, so each Shabraz or Brallin trigger becomes two counters. Knowledge Is Power gives every creature +X/+X for cards drawn this turn, which makes the draw turn the pump turn. Torbran adds 2 to every damage event from a red source to an opponent: each of Brallin's pings becomes 3 (stack 005: seven discards, 21 to each opponent) and by oracle text alone (005 scopes combat out), Brallin's combat damage is a red source too. Artist's Talent at level 3 does the same for noncombat damage, +2 to each ping (stack 004: 21 per seat from seven discards). Its level 1 is a loot per noncreature spell and its level 2 a cost reduction. Whether two draw doublers compound, and how Lae'zel stacks with them, has no passing stack; both are in open_questions.

evidence.note: Torbran's +2 applies to each of Brallin's seven separate pings: 21 to each opponent
Artist's Talent level 3 adds 2 to each of Brallin's seven pings, 21 per seat

stages.label: THE SIDE DAMAGE AND THE CLEARED LANE
stages.what_it_does: What the engine produces besides a large commander. Three bodies collect the same tax: Glint-Horn Buccaneer pings each opponent per discard (a second Brallin), Marauding Mako grows per discard, Chasm Skulker grows per draw and leaves Squids when it dies. deck-audit prices Glint-Horn and Chasm Skulker as single-card components at 7.1% of opening sevens, and Mako sits in the 3-card discard-converter group at 19.9%. None is a plan, only spare damage. Swords to Plowshares and Iroh's Demonstration remove the blocker or the threat that would stop a commander's swing. In the voltron list these are supporting cast; the stage the game turns on is wincon.

stages.label: TWO CREATURES THAT DIE TO ANYTHING
stages.what_it_does: The engine lives in two creatures, so the protection is all commander-centred. Permanent: Lightning Greaves (shroud and haste, equip 0) and Champion's Helm (hexproof on a legend). Held up: Flawless Maneuver (free with a commander out), Loran's Escape, March of Swirling Mist, Negate, Silence (stops the table casting on the kill turn). Recovery: Command Beacon puts a commander from the command zone into your hand, and Campfire does so from the command zone and the graveyard. A commander cast from hand pays no commander tax, so this resets the tax that two removed commanders build up. The declared protection group (8 cards, including Akroma's Will, Boros Charm and Brotherhood Regalia, which this model files under wincon) is drawn by turn six in 79.0% of games (deck-audit). That figure prices drawing these cards, not using them. The goldfish has no removal, so no figure prices any protection card saving a commander, and Forge held Flawless Maneuver as a reactive card.

stages.label: ONE HIT FOR TWENTY-ONE
stages.what_it_does: The game ends on 21 combat damage from one commander. These cards turn the size the engine built into that hit. Double strike: Blade Historian (every attacker, so both commanders), Fireshrieker, Genji Glove (also an extra combat), Lizard Blades, Embercleave (also trample and flash), Akroma's Will (with a commander out: double strike and flying plus the protection mode), Boros Charm. Extra combat: Karlach, Genji Glove. Damage multipliers: Gratuitous Violence doubles damage from your creatures, Fiery Emancipation triples damage from any source you control. Getting through: Brotherhood Regalia and Key to the City make a commander unblockable, Zephyr Boots gives Brallin flying, Inti puts a counter and trample on an attacker. Stoneforge Mystic finds any of the nine Equipment and can put it onto the battlefield for {1}{W}. Stack 001 leaves Shabraz a 10/10 after a seven-card Windfall; no passing stack covers combat, double strike or whether Torbran's and Gratuitous Violence's extra damage counts as commander damage. Every line into this stage is a claim (open_questions).

evidence.note: Blade Historian, Fireshrieker, Genji Glove, Embercleave, Akroma's Will, Boros Charm, Brotherhood Regalia, Gratuitous Violence carry wincon:combat

lines.note: Windfall resolved with both commanders out and seven cards in hand: seven Brallin triggers (1 to each opponent each, 40 to 33), seven Shabraz triggers (+7 counters, +7 life), both end 10/10. None of the fourteen triggers goes on the stack until Windfall has finished resolving. The order is the pilot's thesis: commander first, wheel second.

Artist's Talent's level-3 replacement adds 2 to each of Brallin's seven pings separately: 21 to each seat from Brallin. This is the damage-conversion relation, the same shape as Torbran's, which is why the card is now filed under conversion. The stack never exercises Talent's loot. The Magmakin half of the stack has left the deck; the Brallin half stands.

With Torbran out, each of seven Brallin pings is 1 + 2. Stack 005 stipulates Windfall's seven discards and does not resolve it; that leg rests on stack 001. Result: so 21 to each opponent from Brallin alone, not a kill from 40. The Spider-Man half of that stack has left the deck; the Brallin and Torbran half stands.
CLAIM. Under Teferi's Ageless Insight each of a wheel's draws becomes two, so Shabraz takes two counters per card. No passing stack; how two doublers or Lae'zel stack on top is open.

CLAIM. Brallin's road: Torbran adds 2 and Gratuitous Violence doubles his combat damage. The damaged player orders the two replacements (a ruling input read in stack 005's scope notes), so the defender picks the smaller result; whether all of it is commander damage has no passing stack.

CLAIM. Shabraz's road: a flyer grown by draws, given double strike. Stack 001 leaves him a 10/10, and double strike on a 10/10 is one point short of 21, so the one-turn kill needs one more counter or pump (Lae'zel, Knowledge Is Power, Embercleave's +1/+1). Needs a combat stack.
CLAIM. Greaves (equip 0) lets a commander land and swing protected on the same turn. Stacks 004 and 005 name Greaves only as a card in hand, so they do not verify this.

map_disagreements.why: The map splits the wheels by colour: all five red wheels (Reforge the Soul, which does not burn, among them) sit in CHURN AND MULTIPLY, and the three blue ones (Jace's Archivist, Tolarian Winds, Windfall) in THE BLUE GAS. The engine treats all eight as one fuel, because a discard pays Brallin and a draw pays Shabraz whatever colour the card is.

The neighbourhood THE MULTIPLIERS (city-0-hood-1) puts the draw multipliers (Teferi's Ageless Insight, Alhammarret's Archive, Knowledge Is Power) beside the damage multipliers and double strike (Gratuitous Violence, Fiery Emancipation, Blade Historian), and its gloss reads them all as 'the cards that turn one commander hit into 21'. The engine uses them at two different points: the first three multiply the fuel, the last three multiply the hit. Separately, four of the seven conversion cards (Bard, Lae'zel, Torbran, Artist's Talent) sit in THE CREW, whose gloss is 'the creatures that make them bigger'. So the conversion stage has two addresses. The map does not say why each card went where it did, and this model does not claim a cause.

The kill is one job, 21 from one commander, and it has five addresses on the map. Six Equipment are in THE ARMOURY, and the damage multipliers plus Blade Historian are in THE MULTIPLIERS. Akroma's Will and Boros Charm are in THE INSURANCE, Karlach and Inti in THE CREW, and Key to the City and Stoneforge Mystic in THE HEAD START. That last one is half seen by the map: its neighbourhood ROCKS WITH JOBS (city-1-hood-0) has a gloss that names tutoring equipment and making a commander unblockable. The map places these by what each card is as well as what it does. The engine needs them together on one turn, which is what no city shows.

Shroud on an Equipment (Greaves, Helm) clusters with the other Equipment, recovery on a cheap artifact or land (Campfire, Command Beacon) clusters with the mana, and March of Swirling Mist with the blue cards. THE INSURANCE gets only the held-up instants.
The side damage bodies are filed by colour and type, and the two removal spells by colour. None of it is a coherent city because in this list it is supporting cast, not a plan.
Jeska's Will is a ritual plus exile-three-and-play, and the map reads its card-flow text and colour. Its job is mana for the kill turn.

open_questions.question: With Brallin attacking under Torbran and Gratuitous Violence (and separately Fiery Emancipation), what damage does the defender take, given they order the replacement effects, and is all of it combat damage from a commander for 704.6c?
open_questions.why_it_matters: It is Brallin's whole road to 21. CONTEXT says a rules question found yes, but no passing stack holds it, so every line into wincon from Brallin is a claim.

open_questions.question: Windfall for seven with Shabraz out under Teferi's Ageless Insight plus Bard, King of Dale (or Alhammarret's Archive), with Lae'zel: how many cards are drawn and how many counters land on Shabraz?
open_questions.why_it_matters: Whether two doublers compound decides how large a finishing wheel makes Shabraz, and so whether one double-strike hit is enough.

open_questions.question: A combat stack: Shabraz at 10/10 after stack 001's Windfall, wearing Embercleave or under Blade Historian, attacking one defender. Does it deal 21 or more commander damage, and which single extra (Lae'zel, Knowledge Is Power, Embercleave's +1/+1) takes it over?
open_questions.why_it_matters: It is the deck's primary win and it has no proof at all; stack 001 stops before combat.

open_questions.question: How often is a commander-damage kit (a double-strike piece plus an evasion piece) drawn by turn six and eight, and how often does a commander that is out connect with one?
open_questions.why_it_matters: The commanders' cast rates are priced (goldfish_metrics: both out by turn six in 88.7%), but the voltron kill has no declared group, so nothing prices the wincon stage (see proposed_goldfish_edits).

open_questions.question: Does holding every full-hand wheel until a commander is out beat casting it as soon as it is castable, measured as damage to one seat by turn eight?
open_questions.why_it_matters: The pilot's 'wheels are finishers' rule is what moved the wheels from ignition to fuel. It is a judgment from two games and has not been measured on v2.0.0.

proposed_goldfish_edits.why: Its membership is identical to the wheel group (same eight cards, same measured rates). The six shuffle-or-bottom wheels its label counts all left in v2.0.0.

proposed_goldfish_edits.change: Remove Lae'zel, Vlaakith's Champion (it adds one to each counter placement; it is not a per-draw source) and relabel. Chasm Skulker is the only per-draw body left.

proposed_goldfish_edits.change: Retire both as routes, and add a VOLTRON route: any_of [Blade Historian, Fireshrieker, Genji Glove, Lizard Blades, Embercleave, Akroma's Will, Boros Charm] AND any_of [Brotherhood Regalia, Key to the City, Zephyr Boots, Embercleave, Inti, Seneschal of the Sun, Akroma's Will].

findings.claim: A commander cast from hand pays no commander tax, so this resets the tax that two removed commanders build up
findings.note: NEW, low severity, non-blocking. The first clause is right. 'Resets' is wrong: commander tax counts every earlier cast from the command zone, and a cast from hand does not clear that count. Beacon and Campfire skip the tax for that one cast. If the commander later goes back to the command zone, the next cast from there pays the full accumulated tax again. Also, Command Beacon moves 'your commander' (one card), while Campfire moves 'all commanders you own'. So 'two removed commanders' fits Campfire only. Suggested wording: 'skips the tax for that cast'. No line or figure depends on it.
